verses.english: “These two things, mendicants, are not mortifying.

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, ekaccassa kāyasucaritaṁ kataṁ hoti, akataṁ hoti kāyaduccaritaṁ;
verses.english: It’s when someone has done good things and not done bad things, by way of body, speech, and mind.

verses.pali: vacīsucaritaṁ kataṁ hoti, akataṁ hoti vacīduccaritaṁ;
manosucaritaṁ kataṁ hoti, akataṁ hoti manoduccaritaṁ.
So ‘kāyasucaritaṁ me katan’ti na tappati, ‘akataṁ me kāyaduccaritan’ti na tappati;
verses.english: Thinking, ‘I’ve done good things by way of body, speech, and mind’, they’re not mortified. Thinking, ‘I haven’t done bad things by way of body, speech, and mind’, they’re not mortified.

verses.pali: ‘vacīsucaritaṁ me katan’ti na tappati, ‘akataṁ me vacīduccaritan’ti na tappati;
‘manosucaritaṁ me katan’ti na tappati, ‘akataṁ me manoduccaritan’ti na tappati.
Ime kho, bhikkhave, dve dhammā atapanīyā”ti.
verses.english: These are the two things that are not mortifying.”
